## TL;DR (5 sentences max)
The creator demonstrates how to optimize interior architectural renders in Blender Cycles to achieve production-quality results in under one minute. The workflow focuses on balancing light source placement, using light portals to guide ray tracing, and implementing custom shader setups for windows and curtains. The technique uses the compositor to apply differential denoising to specific objects via Cryptomatte. This produces a clean, photorealistic image without excessive sample counts or long rendering times.

## Workflow sequence (chronological)

1. Set up render parameters (Max Samples, Noise Threshold, Time Limit).
2. Add area light to window for light portal.
3. Configure Light Portal on the area light object.
4. Adjust Window Glass shader using Mix Shader and Light Path (Is Shadow Ray).
5. Adjust Curtain shader using Mix Shader and Light Path.
6. Enable Cryptomatte passes in View Layer settings.
7. Set up Cryptomatte nodes in the Compositor.
8. Use separate Mix nodes for denoising wall objects vs. other scene elements.

## Photorealism techniques (the "secret sauce")

- **Light Portals**: Uses an area light as a light portal to guide samples toward the window, drastically reducing noise in interior scenes with single light sources.
- **Is Shadow Ray shader hack**: Uses the Light Path node to toggle between a reflective surface (glass) and a transparent one (light-passing) depending on the ray type, solving the "dark interior" problem common with standard refractive glass.
- **Object-Specific Denoising**: Uses Cryptomatte masks in the compositor to apply different levels of denoising to walls vs. complex objects, keeping edges sharp while cleaning up noise.

## Common mistakes the creator calls out

- "A common beginner mistake is to just start adding a bunch of lights everywhere." — adding too many lights leads to flat, unrealistic, and washed-out lighting.
- "I don't mean just turning on Denoise." — blanket denoising destroys fine details in textures.

## Direct quotes worth preserving

> "Noise in the rendering is all about light."

> "Glass is complex. It not only blocks light, it refracts and redirects it... for simplicity, the software decided to give it a shadow which is just blocking the light entirely."
